decisions: EVERY NUMBER READS A VIEW. The rebuild happened because the old page summed trips.rate_sar in TypeScript and rendered 0 while Reports rendered 70,650 - rate_sar is NULL on all 203 rows.

A full daily P&L is NOT POSSIBLE. Payroll has no daily source and was 98.9/67.3/74.9 percent of operating cost in Jun/Jul/Aug, so 0104 measures direct_cost_sar only and never calls it cost. Never label direct_margin as profit.
Daily revenue is INVOICING day, not work day. It reads v_revenue_invoices - the same rows the monthly view reads - so days sum to the month by construction, at the cost of a lumpy series.
Delivery Output's bars are capacity DISPATCHED, a proxy. trips.tank_size_m3 is empty on every trip, so a real volume chart would be a flat zero line pretending to be a measurement.

Driver state may have EXACTLY TWO expressions: lib/driver-state.ts and v_driver_state_now. 0103 had embedded a second copy inside v_fleet_state_now; a drivers board would have made a third. The other views compose on it and a drift check asserts the two agree.

active means ASSIGNED (truck + live project), NOT currently driving. Three drivers hold in-flight trips with no assigned truck, so state and trip stage are separate columns and the contradiction is surfaced rather than resolved.
Compliance is four-valued. not_recorded never collapses into ok - five of eleven live drivers have no iqama_expiry and a missing date is not a passing check.
The projects month filter belongs in the LEFT JOIN, never WHERE. Measured on a quiet month: JOIN 6 rows, WHERE 0 rows - the WHERE form blanks every card and reads as an outage.
invoice_unpaid composes on v_receivables_open rather than restating its predicate. The restated version read 5 where Reports read 2. Do not simplify it back.
A failed read may never claim an empty queue. Shipped and fixed: the page rendered 'Every queue is clear right now' while the fetch had errored.
The hero spacer in DashboardClient.tsx is load-bearing - it is the search-bar intro, not decoration. Removing it removes the feature.

The two newest section-7 entries are the DASHBOARD rebuild (migrations 0103-0107, 12 views, sitting after the REPORTS entry because it builds on that semantic layer) and the KANBAN entry, which was rewritten from a stale IN-PROGRESS note. THREE THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) THE DRIFT GUARD'S SHAPE IS THE LESSON: the first one lived behind a throwaway /dash-drift route, became unreachable when that route was deleted at teardown, and was deleted with it. The replacement runs on the Dashboard itself, renders nothing when healthy, and tracks reachable separately from ok because with no session RLS returns zero rows on BOTH sides and a naive comparison would score that as agreement. Do not move it back behind a diagnostic route. (2) CANVAS TEXT IS INVISIBLE TEXT - Chart.js paints its legend onto the canvas, so series names are pixels. ComboChart carries an aria-label and BarChart gained an optional one. Two test bugs came from this: an unscoped getByRole('alert') is never 0 in dev because Next mounts its own empty alert root outside the page tree, and one negative assertion filtered div by text and took .first(), silently resolving to the whole page wrapper - a negative assertion on an unscoped locator proves nothing. (3) THE KANBAN NOTE WAS WRONG IN TWO PLACES, both now corrected in section 7: its 'suspected bug' about unwired STAGE_STYLES tokens was false (s.columnBorder, s.headerText and s.chip all read STAGE_STYLES[stage]), and its item 1 was SUPERSEDED - action buttons are solid-filled in the card's OWN current-stage colour, not the destination's, which is also a deliberate deviation from preview's .kanban-action-*. A future 'match the demo' pass must not revert either. The tests/dashboard-*.spec.ts specs depend on deleted throwaway routes - documentation of what was verified, not a standing suite, same convention as the reports and inventory specs.
